root.name: Benoni Defense: Weenink Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. dxc5 e6

overview: Black meets 3.dxc5 with 3...e6, offering the pawn to regain it with ...Bxc5 and open lines for the pieces. White can develop with Nc3 and e4 while Black recovers the c5 pawn. Play is a normal open queen-pawn game with an even balance; I am unsure of the exact main line.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nc3 and e4 while Black recovers the c5 pawn
Use the centre space gained as Black's bishop comes to c5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black bishop on c5 and White holding c4/e4

character.notes: No known forcing theory; both sides develop normally after the pawn comes back.

gambit.notes: Black regains c5 at once with ...Bxc5, so no lasting material is given.

structure.notes: Tension remains around c4/d4 and the structure is not fixed.

approach.notes: A rare sideline but not one strong players avoid entirely.

level.notes: Ordinary development with no heavy theory.
